:::{#exr-dimension-practice}
#### Finding the dimension of a span that includes a multiple

The [dimension](#def-dimension) of a [span](#def-span) can be smaller than the number of vectors that span it,
for example when one vector is a multiple of another.
Let

$$
\mathcal{S} = \operatorname{span}\cb{\tp{(1, 2, 0)},\ \tp{(2, 4, 0)},\ \tp{(0, 0, 1)}}.
$$

Find $\dim(\mathcal{S})$.

::: {.callout-tip}
#### Hint

Look for a vector in the list that is a multiple of another,
then check that the rest are [linearly independent](#def-linearly-independent).

:::

:::
